subject: Model fit & structured-output evals - next steps + benchmark links
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Model fit & structured-output evals - next steps + benchmark links

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up a short eval/test project: 

Recap of needs (from our call):
- Primary: normalize and enrich transaction records into a fixed JSON schema for downstream risk scoring (high schema fidelity required).
- Throughput/latency targets: ~200 reqs/s peak, p50 < 120ms for 512-token responses (happy to confirm exact SLA in scoping).
- Quality concerns: avoid regressions on merchant extraction and currency rounding; small percent of mis-parses currently causing downstream chargebacks.
- Integration: would prefer function/tool-calling to return typed JSON and a retry-safe idempotency key for intermittent backend failures.

What we propose for an initial eval (2-week sandbox):
1) Recommended models: 
   - rw-instruct-8B (quant-8) - best latency/cost balance for structured output;
   - rw-instruct-16B (fp16) - higher QA for edge cases (subset of traffic);
   - fallback: rw-instruct-3B fast variant for low-cost batch processing.

2) Eval plan and artifacts we'll deliver:
   - shared prompt set + expected JSON schema (we'll validate JSON schema compliance automatically). Link below.
   - benchmark report: token latency, cost/token estimates, accuracy on merchant/category extraction.
   - structured-output tests: schema conformance rate, typical failure modes, and suggested retries/backoff logic.

3) Next steps / asks from your side:
   - share a small sample (>= 2k rows) of anonymized transaction examples (CSV) and any existing schema mapping.
   - confirm whether PCI/PII redaction is required before we ingest samples.
   - schedule a 60-min technical scoping session with Marissa (PM) and Neha (SRE/solutions) - propose Wed or Thu this week.

Links:
- Prompt set & schema (read-only Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-fintech-evals
- Benchmark preview: https://redwood-internal.company/benchmarks/2026Q3-model-comparison

I'll attach the short benchmark deck and a sample JSON schema in the follow-up.

Best,
Rishi

Hi Rishi -

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks like exactly what we need. A few quick answers:
- We'll scrub PII (names/cc) before sending the sample, but include full merchant and amount fields.
- Sample CSV: we'll send 2,500 rows - can you confirm the preferred column headers?
- PCI/compliance: procurement asked that we include a short security questionnaire before samples are shared. Can you loop in our security contact or point us to the SOC2/audit artifacts?

Also - can you confirm how function/tool-calling handles schema validation? If the model returns malformed JSON, do you have automatic retries or a validation+repair pass? We want to avoid downstream failures if the agent returns broken schema.

I'll loop in procurement (procurement@fintechcorp.com) once we have the security artifacts.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model fit & structured-output evals - next steps + benchmark links

Alex - great, appreciate the quick reply. Couple answers inline and a concrete plan: 

On sample CSV headers: our preferred minimal headers are: transaction_id, timestamp, raw_description, amount, currency, merchant_name, merchant_category. We'll accept extras but please include at least these.

Security artifacts: attaching the short SOC2 summary and our standard DPA PDF. For the full SOC2 report we usually run an NDA/SSAE access flow - happy to coordinate with your procurement.

Function/tool-calling & schema handling (short):
- Validation: our eval harness runs a JSON schema validator (the exact schema we'll share). Responses that fail schema are flagged and auto-routed to a repair step.
- Repair step: for typical parse issues we run a deterministic repair policy - either a constrained re-call with clarified prompt (up to 2 auto-retries) or a repair agent that returns a delta to patch the output.
- Idempotency: we include an idempotency key on request metadata so retries are safe server-side; we recommend client-provided ids for best de-duplication.
- Observability: every call logs model output, schema validation result, and repair action, so we can create alerts for regression.

Proposed 2-week sandbox timeline (start next Mon):
- Day 0: share sample CSVs + confirm schema.
- Day 1-3: run baseline benchmarks across rw-instruct-3B/8B/16B (quant/FP variants).
- Day 4-8: run structured-output evals (JSON schema conformance, entity extraction accuracy).
- Day 9-12: edge-case analysis + deploy repair/retry policies on failing prompts.
- Day 13-14: delivery of a report + recommended config (model pinning, batching and caching suggestions, quantization notes).

Attachments: redwood-model-benchmarks-2026Q3.pdf (benchmark primer).

Next step: Alex, can you confirm samples by EOD Thu? Marissa / Neha - can you both confirm availability for the technical scoping call Wed/Thu this week?

Thanks,
Rishi

Looping in a few technical details we'll cover on the scoping call - keeping it high level so procurement has context too: 

1) JSON schema compliance testing approach:
   - We'll provide an OpenAPI-like JSON schema for the transaction payload. During eval we run both strict and lenient validation modes to capture parsing edge cases.
   - Metrics: schema_conformance_rate, field_error_counts, repair_success_rate, and human-review false positive rate.

2) Repair / retry policy specifics:
   - Auto-retries: up to 2 auto-retries with clarified system prompts. Each retry increments a retry_count and logs both outputs.
   - Repair agent: if retries fail, we run a small deterministic repair step (pattern-based fixes) and mark output as 'repaired' with a repair_delta payload.
   - Idempotency: we strongly recommend the client include a stable transaction_id; our runtime attaches an idempotency token to make server-side retries safe.

3) Tool/function-calling considerations:
   - Use tight response schemas and explicit types; prefer enums for merchant_category to reduce variability.
   - For ambiguous descriptions we return both parsed candidates + confidence scores; clients can choose a threshold to escalate to human review.

4) Observability + alerts:
   - We'll set up dashboards for schema_conformance_rate and critical-field-dropouts. If conformance drops 5% vs baseline, automated alert to your SRE/our CS.

Neha - can you run the baseline perf config (rw-instruct-8B quant-8 and rw-instruct-16B fp16) and prepare the first-run results? Alex - we'll share the Drive folder with the schema and prompt set after procurement confirms sample delivery path.

Thanks - looking forward to the scoping call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
